scope: Semantic audit of the 22 v6 variety rows not yet materialized after the first two audit batches. No QR index changes.

policy.rule: Preserve every existing core code and row position. Scientific/taxonomic corrections belong in the knowledge layer.
policy.uncertainty: When authoritative identity or pedigree is unresolved, retain the market/legacy label and mark it pending rather than inventing a pedigree.
policy.bilingual: Chinese and English display forms are retained or proposed; original scientific/official naming is preserved separately when available.

records.finding: IAC research on interspecific coffee germplasm explicitly warns that nomenclature and genetic identity of some materials, especially Aramosa germplasm, can be inconsistent. The core label should therefore not be forced into a simple C. arabica cultivar category.

The name is used in coffee trade, but this audit did not locate an authoritative breeding or accession record sufficient to assign a reliable pedigree. Arusha is also a major Tanzanian geographic name, increasing OCR/entity ambiguity.
World Coffee Research catalogs Bourbon Mayaguez 71 and Bourbon Mayaguez 139 as separate entries. The generic v6 label is therefore not an atomic cultivar identifier.
Cenicafé describes Castillo as a composite variety derived from the Caturra × Timor Hybrid breeding program; it should be modeled as a composite rather than a single homogeneous clone.

records.geneticContext: Advanced progenies from Caturra × Timor Hybrid 1343
Brazilian breeding group with Icatu × Catuaí ancestry; multiple Catucaí selections/cultivars exist
records.finding: The generic v6 Catucaí label should be treated as a breeding/cultivar group. Embrapa documentation for Catucaí selections demonstrates multiple named releases rather than one atomic genotype.

records.finding: Kew POWO accepts Coffea dewevrei as a species and treats Coffea excelsa and Coffea liberica var. dewevrei as synonyms. The old QR text is preserved for compatibility, while the knowledge layer uses the accepted taxon.
IAC maintains multiple Icatu cultivars/lines including red, yellow and early materials. The generic v6 label is therefore an umbrella over multiple registered selections.
WCR confirms JARC as part of Ethiopia's EIAR breeding system; scientific cultivar reviews document 74110 among released Ethiopian cultivars. Parentage is intentionally not inferred here.
CIRAD research describes Laurina/Bourbon Pointu as a spontaneous Bourbon mutation in C. arabica.
Liberica is a Coffea species/market label, not one cultivar. The knowledge model therefore treats this core entry at species level.

Marseillaise appears as a cultivated variety name in published Latin American coffee studies, while authoritative WCR/CIRAD catalogs use the closely related spelling Marsellesa for a defined CIRAD-ECOM Sarchimor line. This audit does not have accession-level evidence proving the two labels are identical.
Mokka/Mocha is used both as a historic coffee/port/style term and as a varietal label in trade. This audit did not locate a sufficiently specific authoritative accession record for the v6 entry.

The market name is well established, but the name alone is not sufficient evidence of Bourbon parentage. The knowledge layer deliberately avoids encoding a Bourbon pedigree without authoritative genetic/accession evidence.
IAC registers specific Red Bourbon material/lines. The generic v6 Red Bourbon entry is useful as a market/color class but should not be assumed to identify one clone or accession.

Sidra is a high-value specialty coffee variety name, but public market descriptions conflict on its origin and parentage. No pedigree is encoded until an authoritative genetic/accession source is registered.
Rume Sudan is used by WCR as a defined Arabica landrace parent in modern breeding pedigrees, including Centroamericano. The v6 naming order Sudan Rume is retained as a market alias.

records.geneticContext: Progeny mixture from Timor Hybrid crossed with Typica/Bourbon-related material

records.finding: The name is established in Ethiopian/specialty coffee usage and appears in scientific germplasm literature, but exact pedigree/accession details were not sufficiently established in the registered primary sources during this audit.
IAC maintains specific Yellow Bourbon accessions/lines. The generic v6 Yellow Bourbon label remains useful as a color/market class but is not one accession.

coverageResult.note: 100% semantic coverage does not mean 100% pedigree certainty; unresolved records remain explicitly pending.
